KPO (Knowledge Process Outsourcing) involves outsourcing knowledge-intensive tasks such as research, analytics and legal or financial analysis, which require specialised domain expertise and higher-level skills.

text: What is touch typing? State one benefit of learning it.
modelAnswer: Touch typing is the technique of typing on a keyboard without looking at the keys, using muscle memory to know the position of each key based on finger placement on the home row. One benefit is that it significantly increases typing speed and accuracy over time.
keyPoints: Touch typing is the technique of typing on a keyboard without looking at the keys, using muscle memory to know the position of each key based on finger placement on the home row.
One benefit is that it significantly increases typing speed and accuracy over time.

text: Name the keys that make up the 'home row' on a standard keyboard and explain their significance.
modelAnswer: The home row consists of the keys A, S, D, F, G, H, J, K, L and the semicolon (;). These keys are significant because fingers rest on this row by default, and all other keys are reached by moving fingers outward from this row and returning to it, which is fundamental to touch typing.
keyPoints: The home row consists of the keys A, S, D, F, G, H, J, K, L and the semicolon (;).

text: How is typing speed measured, and why is accuracy equally important as speed?
modelAnswer: Typing speed is measured in words per minute (WPM), where a 'word' is standardised as five characters including spaces. text: List two common data entry errors and how they can be minimised.
modelAnswer: Two common errors are: (1) transposition errors, where two adjacent characters are swapped (e.g. typing '132' instead of '123'), and (2) omission errors, where a character is missed while typing. These can be minimised through touch typing practice, careful proofreading after data entry, and using data validation rules in spreadsheets to restrict invalid entries.

text: Differentiate between the VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP functions.
modelAnswer: VLOOKUP searches for a value in the leftmost (first) column of a given range and returns a value from a specified column in the same matching row — it is used when data is arranged vertically in columns. HLOOKUP searches for a value in the topmost (first) row of a given range and returns a value from a specified row in the same matching column — it is used when data is arranged horizontally in rows.
keyPoints: VLOOKUP searches for a value in the leftmost (first) column of a given range and returns a value from a specified column in the same matching row — it is used when data is arranged vertically in columns.

text: What is the difference between the SUM and SUMIF functions?
modelAnswer: The SUM function adds up all the numeric values in a specified range unconditionally, e.g. =SUM(A1:A10). The SUMIF function adds up only those values in a range that satisfy a specified condition, e.g. =SUMIF(B1:B10,">50") adds only the values greater than 50.
keyPoints: The SUM function adds up all the numeric values in a specified range unconditionally, e.g. =SUM(A1:A10).

text: Explain the 3 Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) with one example each.
modelAnswer: Reduce means minimising the use of resources or generation of waste, for example buying only what is necessary. Reuse means using an item again for the same or a different purpose instead of discarding it, for example reusing glass jars for storage. Recycle means processing used materials into new products, for example converting waste paper into recycled paper.
keyPoints: Reduce means minimising the use of resources or generation of waste, for example buying only what is necessary.
Reuse means using an item again for the same or a different purpose instead of discarding it, for example reusing glass jars for storage.
Recycle means processing used materials into new products, for example converting waste paper into recycled paper.

text: Suggest any two ways a student can contribute to environmental sustainability in daily life.
modelAnswer: Any two of: switching off lights, fans and other electrical appliances when not in use; using both sides of paper and avoiding wastage of stationery; walking, cycling or using public transport for short distances instead of private vehicles; segregating waste for recycling; planting and caring for trees.
keyPoints: Any two of: switching off lights, fans and other electrical appliances when not in use;
using both sides of paper and avoiding wastage of stationery;
segregating waste for recycling;
planting and caring for trees.

text: Explain briefly how planting trees supports sustainable development.
modelAnswer: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, helping to reduce air pollution and combat climate change. They also help prevent soil erosion, support biodiversity, and maintain the ecological balance, all of which are essential for sustaining natural resources for future generations.
keyPoints: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, helping to reduce air pollution and combat climate change.
